The puzzles are a bit on the easy side generally, and shouldn't give anyone too much trouble. Ultimately, it's closer to a slightly interactive walking simulator than a full fledged point and click adventure game.

If you can pick it up cheap or pick it up as part of a bundle, and generally enjoy this type of game, you can give it a shot. Otherwise, there's just not enough here.

Dead Secret is an interesting game. It's short and linear, but it kept me interested all the way through. I played this on PC, without VR.

Dead Secret é um jogo de mistério com elementos de terror no qual o jogador controla uma repórter investigando o possível assassinato de um recluso professor. O jogo claramente foi feito para ser jogado com um headset VR, com uma interface bem minimalista e até um pouco não convencional, e considerando o ano que ele saiu e as reviews da crítica na época assumo que ele fez certo sucesso quando saiu. Por mais que pareça mesmo que a experiência seria melhor se eu tivesse jogado ele em VR, a conversão para desktop acaba transformando esse jogo em um point-and-click 3D, com você clicando para se mover pelo cenário e interagir com objetos.

A história aqui é um "whodunnit", com o jogador lendo as dúzias de notas, páginas de diário e cartas espalhadas pelo cenário para entender o que está ocorrendo e apontar quem foi o assassino. Eu me surpreendi que o jogo implementou alguns elementos de survival horror, especialmente inspirados em Clock Tower, que por mais que sejam simples e leves ajudam na atmosfera aqui. Eu comecei achando a história bem simplista, e por mais que nunca se torne algo extremamente complexo, você acaba descobrindo elementos da história que tornam fatos apresentados antes mais interessantes em retrospectiva.

Eu recomendo Dead Secret pra quem quer um point-and-click de mistério e com leves elementos de terror pra jogar em uma sessão só, ele pode ser encerrado com todos seus finais em torno de 3 horas - e especialmente para quem tem um headset VR, por mais que imagino que ele seja bem antiquado para os padrões de jogos de realidade virtual atuais, ainda assim me parece uma experiência divertida e imersiva para jogar usando ele.

This is a pretty straightforward murder mystery adventure game, but it has some fun 'scares' that might make you classify this as horror or thriller. The walking mechanic is non-existent, like old-school adventure games where you click the 'edge' of a scene to move in that direction... that makes some of the 'scare' scenes extra tense because you don't get to mash a RUN button! The puzzles were simple and fun, and I say this as someone who does not like complex puzzle games. I hate having to check a guide for every unintuitive step, and I did not need a guide for this one. The masks were used marvelously, the scariest one for the most helpful character kept a nice, creepy vibe throughout the game. I had just gotten a really gnarly painting of a monster face set up beside my computer, and I keep seeing it out of the corner of my eye while playing. This game helped to convince me I needed to install it somewhere else. Aha! Get the game if you want to experience a short (2-3) hour spooky tale.

Hororová adventura od malého nezávislého studia Robot Invader. Hra je primárně určena pro virtuální realitu, ale lze ji hrát i klasicky na monitoru s klávesnicí a myší... či spíše jen myší. :) Ovládání je totiž řešeno tak nějak postaru, jako u starých 3D adventur po skocích. Nepohybujete se volně, ale kliknete do určitého směru, postava pár kroků popojde, pak kliknete do dalšího směru, postava zase popojde pár kroků tím směrem. Je to trochu zastaralé a nepohodlné, ale dá se na to zvyknout. Levou ruku vůbec nepoužíváte, tak si můžete v klidu dávat kafe, nebo chroupat brambůrky. ;)
Příběh se má tak, že je rok 1965, jste reportérka Patricia Gable a jdete do jednoho opuštěného domu někde v kansaských polích vyšetřit záhadnou smrt podivného vědce. Vědec, pracující na podivných tajemných výzkumech, týkajících se lidské mysli, během léta umrznul - podivné, že? :) Příběh vám vypráví tuny a tuny papírů, válejících se všude kolem. Stránky denníčku, dokumenty, atd... Příběh je opravdu hodně propracovaný a povedený. Na závěr vás čeká celkem 5 konců, podle toho, koho určíte za vraha a co s ním pak uděláte.
Hra se ukládá sama jen při ukončení. Po dohrání vás tlačítko "Continue" hodí před závěrečné rozhodnutí, takže se můžete libovolně podívat na všechny konce. Hra má cca 3,5 hodiny, ale návod jen 40 minut, ale za tuhle dobu to dohraje je ten, kdo už hru zná a ví, co má kde dělat.
Plusy:
Skvělá hororová atmosféra v opuštěném domě. Venku prší, ozývají se podivné zvuky a občas je i nějaká lekačka. V domě totiž jaksi nejste sami. :)
Propracovaný příběh.
Mínusy:
Grafika (Unity engine) je docela mdlá a nedetailní. Asi úlitba virtuální realitě - aby se to hýbalo.
Ve hře není vůbec žádné grafické a zvukové nastavení. Uvítal bych možnost snížit alespoň hlasitost hudby.
Systém pohybu pomocí klikání myší je celkem nepohodlný, ale dá se na něj zvyknout.
V jednom místě je technický bug, kvůli kterému nelze pokračovat dál (po vlezení do tmavého sklepa). Naštěstí se stačí vrátit do hlavního menu a dát pokračovat.
Na hru bohužel není čeština a porozumět dokumentům, které vytváří příběh, je ke hraní nutné, takže jestli neumíte anglicky, tak máte smůlu. Hra by si češtinu rozhodně zasloužila. Doporučuji alespoň český letsplay půvabné české youtuberky MsRepulsive, která dokumenty během hraní překládá. :)

Very atmospheric, slow-paced mystery adventure in the form of a first-person point-and-click investigation game. You are an aspiring journalist in a backwater town, and this is your chance. It's not exactly a horror experience, but it's definitely a thriller - similar to The Painscreek Killings, albeit much more claustrophobic. It's very condensed, too - no wasted space, no fillers.

[b][u]PROS - story, music, atmosphere[/u][/b]

It's a very cosy game, at least at the beginning. Autumn evening in the middle of nowhere, pattering rain and croaking ravens, chill music and faint creaking of the old house. The ambient soundcape is ominous and thick, amplifying suspense and psychological tension. There is a great attention to details, both visual and sound cues. Properly mind-boggling and nuanced story, with unexpected twists and turns, becomes very unsettling towards the end, as the sun sets and the moon rises.

Lens mechanics, though cool, feels underutilized. It's mainly used for hints. Puzzles are very simple and seemingly exist only for the sake of progression. The gameplay/investigation is still based on pixel-hunting, finding various notes, items and documents, but the story is presented in quite a clever way. The game features a number of jumpscares, but they are all quite fitting.


[b][u]CONS: technical issues, voice acting, some questionable plot points[/u][/b]

Dead Secret was made with VR in mind and it shows. Limited movement (pre-determined points), strange inventory system, simplified visuals with low-res textures. Yet it still plays and feels just fine in traditional non-VR, so that's more of a nitpick.

The game seems to hate multi-monitor setup, and there is no way to change graphical settings in options. You have to hold Shift while the game launches to access the settings dialog window. Seriously, for a 2016 game, this kind of technical design decisions is extremely frustrating.

It also is a mess on Steam Deck. All in-game animations are tied to the framerate and it needs to run in at least 60 fps, otherwise there are bad audio sync issues, slow movement and other bugs (many of which still persist, though). Add [code]-show-screen-selector[/code] in launch properties for the settings window to appear.

The UI has that specific VR style and is clunky in general. Inventory items, readable documents and system options are all arranged in a 3D wheel shape, floating in a black void. There are far too many categories for collected documents - when you want to reread something, good luck guessing in which category it is. It's like rummaging through real dusty archive binders.

The voice acting is flat and often sounds like an AI generated voice.

There is some questionable characterization of a particular person - some of their actions don't fit into their personality or aren't properly explained/justified, and seemingly exist only for another character's motivation, and thus plot twist, to happen.


[b]Conclusion[/b]

I thoroughly enjoyed Dead Secret. Technical issues and minor nitpicks aside, I highly recommend this little game for the fans of the genre. This fascinating [spoiler]murder mystery with a bit of supernatural[/spoiler] is perfect for a slow evening.

[h1][b]Dead Secret[/b][/h1]


[b]Summary:[/b]
Harris Bullard’s death has been passed off as due to ‘natural causes’, but something seems [i]off[/i] about all of this. As an ambitious journalist looking for her big break, you must uncover the truth about what happened to Bullard, and keep yourself alive long enough to do so.

[h2]The Good:[/h2]
-	[b]The mystery[/b]: I think this mystery is a hit! Everyone has a reason to want this man dead—some are better reasons than others—but by using logic it will become clear who did the crime and why.
-	[b]Lore[/b]: If you are one of those people who reads every codex entry then this is the game for you. Document after document hints at which way to turn, and how to keep yourself safe. Not to mention there’s a fair bit of hilarity in them upon occasion too.
-	[b]The atmosphere[/b]: The setting seemed so empty, but in a good way. It’s really reminiscent of a house that isn’t being lived in [i] anymore [/i], but in a place that was once meaningful and lived-in.  
-	[b] Linearity [/b]: I really appreciate that most clues helped lead you to the next clue. They don’t give you an object or a hint and then just ignore it for 4/5ths of the game.
-	[b]The spooks: [/b]I was spooked! 
-	[b] The truth [/b]: was worth solving!

[h2]The Not So Good: [/h2]
-	[b]Clicking[/b] – The bane of my existence in this game. Can I click this? Or this? Or this? Or this? The answer is mostly no!

A murder has taken place, will more happen?  Use your investigative skills to unlock the mystery of the murder of Harris Bullard and uncover the enigma of his mysterious invention.  Who murdered the strange professor?  Was it the estranged ex-wife, the new assistant, the former research partner, the errand boy, or something else entirely?

Dead Secret is a first-person horror mystery set in rural Kansas in the 1960s.  Playing as a reporter you investigate a death of the prominent professor; searching his home for clues by clicking items, sometimes combining them, and progressing from there.  For the most part you will be moving from room to room solving puzzles and finding items that will unlock further mysteries within the house.  The puzzles are relatively straightforward and require some thinking and deductive reasoning along with a good eye for clues.

While the world is three dimensional, the game sometimes feels like a point-and-click game; for example, moving from one spot to another requires clicking in that direction after which the game will walk you over there.  The traveling method feels a bit cumbersome and not very intuitive as I found myself trying to walk around on my own quite often.  It is important to note that the game was originally designed for VR, and as such, some of the features seem a bit off.  With that aspect of the game known, Dead Secret can be played without VR—which was my experience with the game.

The story of Dead Secret is very well done.  Monologues and found papers all tell the story and deepen the mystery—for those who like to blast past the reading part of games you probably will not get what is going on but for those who take the time to read the notes you are in for a real treat.  I enjoyed learning more about the different off-screen characters and was thoroughly engrossed with the mystery.

Achievements are easy to get—with Dead Secret being the first game where I didn’t have to replay the entire story to get the alternate endings; you just need to start from the last game save.  Sadly, there are only five achievements for Dead Secret and I would have liked to have seen more achievements but was grateful for what was given.

The controls were okay but understanding that the game was originally designed for VR—they are not bad.  I found myself going back and forth between the keyboard and the controller with little change in efficiency or ease.

Dead Secret is not a bad game…I found it quite enjoyable.  And while short; the game does lend itself to the horror mystery genre and I found myself invested in the enigma and was delightfully terrified with several sequences.  I recommend this game for those who like either genres or for those looking for a quick game to play.

You are a newspaper reporter who has been relegated to nothing but fluff pieces, but you have discovered a strange story that has been ruled a suicide, but to you there seems to be something fishy about it. So on a whim you decide to explore the house of Professor Harris Bullard, and this is where your adventure into Dead Secret begins. 

The game is in first person perspective and you can definitely tell that VR was part of the equation. The game has an option to have a controller, but I think the developer had the controller setup that goes with a VR system in mind. When I tried to play with a standard gamepad the game felt almost unplayable. So I went with your standard click of the mouse to do the interactions. I have to admit that even going that route still caused some clunkiness to occur when trying to play with a little bit of finesse. There are times where you want to interact with something but because of how you clicked on the screen to move you’ll walk right past it and will have to try from different angles. The interesting thing is that even with the frustration that came with this I kept with the game, there was enough there that I kept going.

The majority of the game is centered around solving puzzles and collecting information. Some of the puzzles you can solve right away while some of them will require multiple steps to complete. I will admit that I didn’t end up solving all of the puzzles, but I was able to complete the game. Now I also mentioned that you’ll be collecting information, and you’ll be using the information that you find to determine what may have actually happened to Professor Bullard. There are a couple of different characters that interacted with the professor near his death, and it is up to you to figure out if any are guilty of killing him.

This wasn’t actually that long of a game, but I definitely feel like I got my money’s worth. There were a couple of times during the game where you will have to start over from an autosaved checkpoint, but to not ruin some of the twists I won’t reveal why these occur, just believe me when I say you’re not going to see it coming. This is also a tough game to recommend or say STAY AWAY. I think you would probably have a better experience if you are able to go the VR route, but don’t quote me on that. I really really liked the story, it was well crafted. It had plenty of twists and turns that will keep you guessing up to the very end. So if you’re looking for a very well crafted story with a game that can be pretty clunky at times I would tell you to get this game. If you have issues playing a game where you notice right off the bat that the controls are going to be a struggle then save yourself some grief and avoid this game. As I stated before even though I had some serious issues with the controls from time to time, I enjoyed the game.

Une maison reculée au fin fond du Kansas. Une étrange affaire de meurtre. Des recherches étranges, presque ésotériques. Une journaliste déterminée à trouver le scoop de sa vie. Et une silhouette inquiétante qui rôde...

Dead Secret est un jeu d'enquête - avant tout pensé pour la VR! Donc, un système de déplacement assez rigide (très surprenant quand on est pas habitué) et des graphismes qui reste relativement sommaire.
On fouille la maison, tentant de reconstituer la suite des événements ayant mené à la mort du locataire des lieux, résolvant des énigmes... en tentant d'échapper à un mystérieux être masqué, qui veut nous faire payer notre curiosité. On est pas dans un Kholath ou Amnesia, cette apparition est scriptée et si l'apercevoir est signe de danger, c'est aussi signe que l'on progresse...
Le surnaturel s'invite aussi à la fête, notamment via la présence de mystérieuses lunettes nous donnant des "indices" et le thème de la Yuki-Onna qui semblait hanter la psychée du défunt. Mais, et c'est assez frustrant, cet aspect des choses ne sera jamais approfondie! On sait que ça a un lien avec les recherches du défunt, mais rien de bien concret...

Le jeu est relativement court, même si certaines énigmes sont assez difficiles. Le prix pourrait sembler légèrement excessif... sauf si on prend en compte l'aspect VR, les jeux utilisant cette technologie étant généralement bien plus cher que la moyenne.

This game is in a tough spot.  Kind of mild survival horror, I guess, and it's easy to dismiss since there's nothing major that stands out.  It looks ok but not great.  The puzzles get the job done but you're not going to remember any of them for very long.  It's kind of eerie, but it won't exactly give you nightmares.

It does a lot of small things right, though, in ways you wouldn't necessarily expect.

The investigative reporter angle, for instance.  Some games will start off with a device like that as an excuse to jump start the plot and then forget about it; but here they keep it up from start to finish.  I liked that aspect, where you're scribbling down notes with a pencil, reviewing the evidence in your little notebook and piecing a story together around each suspect.  It added another layer of immersion and made solving the mystery feel more concrete.

Like i said, it's not really that scary.  Sort of medium-creepy; but once again they bring some unique stuff to the table.  The 1960s setting, for one.  The deserted farmhouse out in the middle of nowhere in Kansas is a pretty great place for a game like this, one that you don't see all the time.  You're walking around the house, staring out across a wide open field under a gray sky, listening to the raindrops patter against the window and the crows squawk outside, and it does set a foreboding mood.  

They make good use of silence, especially at the beginning when you're not sure what's going on yet.  Actually, by the end I still wasn't sure whether there was supposed to be something paranormal happening or not.  They hand-waved a bunch of stuff about the subconscious or whatever, but it most of the time it seemed more like magic.  Either way, I appreciated that they tried to do something different there.

When you think about it, they could have just made Generic Horror Game #357,249 to capitalize on the VR fad, but they actually came up with some novel ideas and made a real effort to carry them out in a consistent way.

That's the story of this game, I guess.  On the surface it seems like nothing special, but if you're willing to be a little bit charitable you can find some real virtues here.

Except for that monkey.  #%@& him.

The VR implementation worked out better than I at first thought it would.  There is no real locomotion (I played on Vive)--instead you click a spot and glide across the scene to the new location.
